category_feedback.specific_evidence: expanded_walkthrough.title = 'When the child cuts the leftover cookie in HALF for a 3-friend share — repairing the fraction-mismatch error' and recovery_moves include 'match the fraction to the sharers' mantra and pizza-overlay repair, but the rationale and recovery do not cite named fraction-misconception research (e.g., Empson & Levi on equipartitioning, or Steffe & Olive on partitive vs. quotitive division). The branching by diagnostic ('If the child STILL defaults to halves: the rule hasn't connected to the WHY') is good but not anchored to a research-named principle.
category_feedback.required_fix: Add a one-line research citation in expanded_walkthrough.rationale anchoring the fraction-mismatch trap to named research — e.g., 'This is the equipartitioning failure described in Empson & Levi (2011) Extending Children's Mathematics: children apply a 'cut-in-half' default learned from 2-sharer Grade 1 work to all leftover splits, regardless of the sharer count.' This pushes the trap from Level 3 (real misconception with concrete recovery) to Level 4 (research-grounded).

category_feedback.specific_evidence: lesson_specific_materials lists 'Per-group set of 12+ paper cookies (some pre-cut along third-line, some along sixth-line)' and 'Pizza fraction cards: whole, thirds (3 sectors), sixths (6 sectors), with same-size whole pizzas for overlay demos' as required. The differentiation.for_movement_learners offers a kinesthetic option ('allow them to BE the dealer at every station') but this still requires paper cookies and plates. There is no explicit no-paper / no-prep alternative path using only voice, body, gesture, or items already in any G2 classroom (e.g., counters, bottle caps, fingers as 'sharers').
category_feedback.required_fix: Add a no-paper, no-prep variant in differentiation. Concrete example: 'No-materials version — use 7 bottle caps (or counters/erasers) as cookies and 3 children's open hands as plates. For the leftover, draw a circle on chart paper and cut/erase three pie-wedges with marker. Pizza overlay can be replaced by two same-size paper plates from the lunchroom, folded into thirds vs. sixths and held one in front of the other.' This converts Level 3 to Level 4 by guaranteeing the lesson runs on a no-prep day.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: Conceptual progression is explicit and Station C invites comparison ('Try to find ALL the equivalences. Some pairs are equal; some aren't.'), which is genuine strategy refinement. However, the expanded_walkthrough names the misconception in everyday terms ('the leftover always gets cut in half. Grade-1 strategy holdover') without citing the fraction-research literature. Level 4 requires 'names the misconception in research-grounded terms (Carpenter & Moser CGI types, Empson on fractions, Battista on spatial reasoning, etc.).'
category_feedback.required_fix: Either in expanded_walkthrough.rationale or in pedagogical_notes, name the principle in research-grounded terms. Suggested wording: 'Empson & Levi (2011) describe the developmental progression in equipartitioning: children first master 2-share/halving, then must coordinate the number of shares with the fraction name. The cut-in-half default is the predictable transition error when 3-share or 6-share situations arrive — children import their halving schema. The repair is to make the share-count-to-fraction-name mapping explicit BEFORE cutting.' Pairs naturally with the pedagogical_depth fix above.
